# Replit Agent at a glance

Replit Agent is an AI software builder inside Replit that can plan, design, code, debug, and publish applications from natural-language requests. Its all-in-one workspace is convenient for prototypes and production-oriented builds, but Agent, hosting, databases, and integrations draw from shared credits, so teams need active cost controls and hands-on testing.

[Visit the official Replit Agent site ↗](https://replit.com/)

Overview

## What Replit Agent is

Replit Agent combines an AI coding agent with a hosted development environment, visual design tools, databases, integrations, collaboration, and publishing. Users can begin with an idea, an existing project, a screenshot, or a design, then ask Agent to create and modify working software.

Plan Mode lets users review scope, success criteria, and implementation steps before files change. Build Mode can write and edit code, run commands, debug errors, and create checkpoints, while the Visual Editor and Design Canvas provide more direct control over layout and content.

Replit’s billing model is broader than a flat AI subscription. Paid Agent work uses effort-based pricing, and subscription credits also cover cloud services such as published apps, storage, databases, and some third-party AI integrations. A project can therefore cost more than its base plan if Agent or infrastructure usage exceeds the included credits.

Use cases

## Who Replit Agent is best for

The strongest fit depends on the job you need the product to complete, not the size of its feature list.

### Full-stack prototypes

Turn a clear product brief into a hosted application with interface, server logic, storage, authentication, and deployment in one environment.

### Non-specialist builders

Product managers, founders, designers, and operators can collaborate with Agent while still inspecting the plan, preview, code, and checkpoints.

### Small product teams

Core and Pro include multiple collaborators, shared workspaces, task planning, and background Agent work without separate per-seat pricing within plan limits.

### Fast experiments

Build landing pages, dashboards, internal tools, chatbots, mobile apps, slides, data visualizations, and other artifacts without assembling a separate toolchain first.

Capabilities

## Core Replit Agent features

1

### Plan and Build modes

Plan Mode prepares a reviewable approach before code changes, while Build Mode executes tasks and records completed work in checkpoints.

2

### Autonomous coding agent

Agent can plan changes, write code, run commands, explain behavior, debug failures, and iterate on an application.

3

### Design Canvas and Visual Editor

Users can explore visual directions, annotate designs, convert designs into artifacts on paid plans, and directly edit page content and layout.

4

### Built-in app infrastructure

Replit provides hosted workspaces, databases, storage, authentication options, secrets, logs, and multiple publishing approaches inside the same platform.

5

### Checkpoints and rollback

Agent checkpoints capture changes and can restore files, Agent memory, tasks, and optionally databases when a build goes in the wrong direction.

6

### Connectors and AI integrations

Paid plans can connect third-party services, while some generated apps can use provider APIs such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini through Replit-managed billing.

7

### Parallel background work

Current plans support two parallel agents on Core and ten on Pro, with additional collaboration and task-planning features.

8

### Integrated publishing

Starter includes one published project for 30 days, while Core and Pro support unlimited published projects with infrastructure usage billed through credits.

# Effort-Based Pricing Recap

![Effort-Based Pricing Recap — cover image](https://cdnimg.replit.com/images/bj34pdbp/migration/274c794eb0d273c0d1a7bc1765f6f411fb6e18f9-4172x2190.png?w=3840&q=80&fit=max&auto=format)

Published:

Jul 12, 2025

Updated:

Jul 14, 2025

![The Replit Team](https://cdnimg.replit.com/images/bj34pdbp/migration/1caa9c698f108ffd46cd8119f002386c8daeb885-400x400.jpg?w=3840)

The Replit Team

On June 18th, we enabled a new pricing feature called [Effort-Based Pricing](https://blog.replit.com/effort-based-pricing) for all newly signed up Replit users. After monitoring usage for two weeks, we began rolling this feature out to the remaining users last week on July 2nd. In this post, we would like to share more about the rationale for the change, what we have observed so far, address some of our users’ concerns, and share how we are continuing to improve pricing.

We are confident that the new Effort-Based pricing is the model that will best serve our users and enable more powerful AI tools to Replit members, however the transition to the new pricing model did not meet our standards for how we like to roll out major changes (we will discuss some examples of areas where we fell short). Therefore, we would like to offer $10 in free Replit credits to all Replit members who used the new pricing model as a way to show that we appreciate your feedback and your patience during this transition. This will automatically be applied to all active accounts that have used the new pricing model. There is nothing that users need to do to claim this credit.

## July 11th Incident:

One example of where we fell short in our rollout of the pricing happened on July 11th between the hours of 11:26AM PDT - 5:43PM PDT. During this time, and due to an error in cost calculation, Replit checkpoint charges were being incorrectly computed and were often much larger than they should have been. After 5:43PM the fix was rolled out to production. This impacted approximately 6% of paying users. We have performed a thorough incident analysis, ensured that all charges related to the incident are refunded/credited, and have applied additional guardrails to make sure that this doesn’t happen again.

We apologize for this July 11th incident and we thank our community members for helping us identify this issue. We were able to determine exactly who was impacted, by how much, and will automatically issue refunds or credits to any user that was impacted by this error. There is nothing that these users need to do to initiate the refund. The total cost of all impacted checkpoints will be reimbursed. Impacted users will also receive an email explaining what has happened.

These refunds will be in addition to the additional $10 in credits that we are offering to all active Replit members who have been using the new Effort-Based Pricing.

The pricing that people experienced during this incident was not representative of what people are normally charged under the new Effort-Based Pricing feature. The rest of this article will focus on how Effort-Based Pricing works, how charges are calculated, and how that differs from the previous pricing model. We will also highlight some optimizations we’ve recently made to reduce the Replit costs for all users.

## How Agent Works:

When Agent receives a message from users, it uses AI models along with automated testing to build, modify, and test the user’s application. Periodically, Agent will create “snapshots” of the project called checkpoints. Checkpoints allow users to browse the history of the application or roll back / preview previous versions. Since checkpoints represent concrete units of work, we use them as opportunities to bill users for their usage.

At Replit, we’re building a fully automated software developer so you can eventually create any software you can imagine. The first version of Agent (v1) that came out of beta in Dec 2024, could only work for up to a couple of minutes at a time. So it made sense to generate a single checkpoint and bill the user a flat rate of $0.25, which at the time was enough to cover the cost of AI and running the service.

With v2, however, Replit can run autonomously for up to 20 minutes. This was a huge upgrade that meant people could build entire businesses on Replit and automate large swaths of work. In this world, the one-message-one-checkpoint model no longer worked because 20 minutes of work could cost us upwards of $10.

Therefore, we patched the Agent to generate a checkpoint every ninth time that the Agent ran a command behind the scenes. That was a heuristic that “felt right,” but in reality, it rarely aligned with the actual work or value being delivered. It also generated a lot of intermediate, superfluous checkpoints that polluted the project history, making it harder to roll back or preview old changes. So that had to change.

## What Has Changed With Effort-Based Pricing?

**Previously:**

*   In general, one request to Agent would result in at least one checkpoint.
*   These checkpoints were performed at times that were not meaningful.
*   Each checkpoint would cost the user $0.25.

**With new Effort-Based Pricing:**

*   Agent will create at most one checkpoint per request instead of many.
*   On average, that checkpoint will represent _more_ work performed by Agent.
*   The cost per checkpoint is now determined based on the amount of computing resources consumed.
*   Simpler requests may cost as little as $0.06 and more involved requests will usually cost more than $0.25, sometimes resulting in charges of multiple dollars depending on the size of the work.

A few of the most noticeable changes users have observed under Effort-Based Pricing are as follows.

1.  Users have seen checkpoint charges as low as $.06 where that same request would have cost _more_ under the old pricing model (at least $0.25).
2.  Users have seen checkpoints costing over $1, and they would have been charged the same amount under the old pricing model.
3.  Users have seen checkpoints costing over $1, and they would have been charged _less_ under the old pricing model.

![effort-based-pricing-comparison](https://cdn.replit.com/sanity/blog/EffortBasedPricingComparisonV2.png)

## What We Have Observed In The Data:

As we rolled out the new pricing, we tracked the median checkpoint price and we observed that it only went up slightly vs the old pricing model. That meant for most users the cost didn’t move all that much. However, we hadn’t appreciated how much it affected power users.

Some increase in median checkpoint price was expected because Effort-Based checkpoints, on average, pack in more work. However, Effort-Based pricing can end up being more expensive over the lifetime of a project, and median stati

# Replit pricing explained (2025)

As of March 2025, Replit’s pricing structure has evolved to match its growing capabilities, offering plans for everyone—from curious beginners to sprawling development teams.

**Not using Replit yet? Get $10 extra credit when you signup with** **[this link](https://replit.com/refer/andrewjdavison)****.**

But with new features, AI tools, and deployment options comes a need to understand how much it’ll cost you to harness Replit’s power. Don’t worry, we’ve got you covered! In this blog post, we’ll break down Replit’s plans, dive into AI and deployment costs, and highlight recent changes—all while keeping things engaging and easy to follow. Let’s jump in!

## Understanding Replit’s Plans

Replit offers four distinct plans to suit a variety of users: **Starter**, **Replit Core**, **Teams**, and **Enterprise**. Each comes with its own perks, pricing, and target audience. Here’s the rundown.

### Starter Plan: Free and Beginner-Friendly

New to coding or just kicking the tires? The [Starter plan](https://replit.com/pricing) is your entry point—and it’s totally free. You get basic access to Replit’s platform, including limited use of its slick AI features like the Replit Agent. You can also create up to three public apps to share with the world. It’s a fantastic way to dip your toes in, but if you want private apps or more robust AI tools, you’ll need to level up. Think of it as the “try before you buy” option—perfect for students or hobbyists starting small.

### Replit Core: The Developer’s Choice

For solo developers or serious coders, the [Replit Core plan](https://replit.com/pricing) is where things get exciting. Priced at **$20 per month (billed annually)** or **$25 per month**, this plan unlocks the full Replit experience. You get unlimited public and private apps, full access to AI tools like the Replit Agent and advanced models (think Claude Sonnet 3.7 and OpenAI GPT-4o), and the ability to deploy live projects. The real kicker? It comes with **$25 in monthly credits** to spend on AI usage, deployments, and other cloud services—enough for about 100 Agent checkpoints. Bonus: Replit bumped those credits up from $10 to $25 in February 2025 without hiking the price. That’s a win for power users who need more juice for their projects!

### Teams Plan: Collaboration Made Easy

Got a squad of coders? The [Teams plan](https://replit.com/pricing) is built for you, clocking in at **$40 per user per month**. It includes everything from Replit Core, plus extras like centralized billing, role-based access control, and private deployments. Each user also gets **$40 in monthly credits**, making it a solid choice for organizations that need to scale up and streamline collaboration. Whether you’re a startup or a classroom, Teams keeps everyone on the same page—literally and figuratively.

### Enterprise Plan: Custom Solutions for Large Organizations

Big teams with big needs turn to the [Enterprise plan](https://replit.com/pricing). Pricing here is custom, tailored to your organization’s specific requirements. Expect features like single sign-on (SSO), advanced security options, and dedicated support. It’s the premium package for companies that need Replit to fit like a glove—perfect for large-scale operations where flexibility and performance are non-negotiable.

## AI Features and Costs

Replit’s AI tools are a standout feature, turning your coding sessions into a sci-fi movie where you’ve got a brilliant assistant by your side. But brilliance comes at a cost—luckily, one you can manage with your monthly credits. Let’s break it down.

### Replit Agent: Pay Per Checkpoint

The Replit Agent is like having a coding sidekick that automates tasks and tweaks your files. You’re charged **$0.25 per checkpoint**, which happens every time the Agent makes a change—whether it finishes the job or not. New users get **10 free checkpoints** to play with, and on the Core plan, your $25 credits cover up to 100 checkpoints monthly. It’s a powerful tool, but keep an eye on those checkpoints to avoid burning through your credits too fast!

### Advanced Assistant: Affordable Coding Help

Need a quick fix or a feature built? The Advanced Assistant has your back, costing just **$0.05 per edit request**. New users snag **20 free requests** to start, and the credits from Core or Teams plans can cover plenty more. There’s also a free Basic Assistant mode, but it’s less capable—think of it as the lite version. For the real deal, stick with Advanced. You can track all this usage in the Agent or Assistant tabs or on the [usage page](https://replit.com/account#resource-usage)—just note that updates might lag by up to 30 minutes.

## Deployment and Database Billing

Replit isn’t just about coding; it’s about getting your projects live. That means deployments and databases, which come with their own usage-based billing. Recent tweaks in February 2025 shook things up a bit, so let’s simplify the techy details.

### Deployment Types and Costs

Replit offers a buffet of deployment options, each with its own pricing flavor:

*   **Outbound Data Transfer**: Charged per byte, but Replit Core users get **100 GiB of free egress** monthly. Overages are **$0.10 per GiB**, and only outgoing data counts—your incoming traffic is free.
*   **Autoscale Deployments**: These scale with demand and are billed via **Compute Units** (CPU and RAM usage). For example, 1 RAM second = 2 units, and 1 CPU second = 18 units. Overages cost **$1 per million Compute Units**, and a new **$1/month base fee** hit in February 2025 (same goes for Scheduled Deployments).
*   **Requests**: Extra costs depend on how many requests your app handles—check the [pricing page](https://replit.com/pricing) for the latest rates.
*   **Other Options**:
    *   **Reserved VM Deployments**: Start at **$10/month** for consistent performance.
    *   **Scheduled Deployments**: Run on a timer for **$0.000061/second**.
    *   **Static Deployments**: Free up to 100 GiB of outbound data with Replit Core—perfect for simple sites.

### Database Billing (PostgreSQL)

Replit’s serverless PostgreSQL databases are handy, but they’re not free. Costs come from:

*   **Compute Time**: Charged per hour your database is active (any request or within 5 minutes of the last one).
*   **Data Storage**: Billed for total stored data, capped at **10 GiB per database**, with a **33MB default footprint** even if it’s empty.

Your monthly credits cover these costs, with overages billed separately. Peek at your usage on the [account usage page](https://replit.com/account#resource-usage) to stay in control.
